design:
D1. Which notices exist, and what each one does (owner: OverviewScreen.tsx, the container; OverviewView.tsx stays presentational).
- Question, asker waiting: inline options or Open conversation, plus Decline. Question, asker gone: Decline; section-level decline-all for these. Owner of the action: the existing decline route (questions.py:640), looped by the UI; no new route for 28 calls.
- Blocked task: Resume work / Open task (slice B), plus an error toast.
- Approved but not merged: driven by open integration_* stalls (see D2). Try again (existing integrations/retry route) when latest_integration.retryable; Dismiss ends the stall.
- Other stall: Open thread/task + Dismiss (exists), plus an error toast.
- Flaky tests: Create a fix task / Dismiss (exists), plus an error toast.
- Couldn't-read line: Retry (refetch of the failed queries); clears itself on success.
- Budget exhausted: link to Budgets (exists); clears itself when the budget is not exhausted.
- Agent chips: 'no charter', 'no runner', 'can't run' already link to their fix; 'held by hop budget' becomes a link to Project settings > General; 'launch not checked' and 'queue not read' clear themselves on a successful read.
- CheckpointStatusBanner (every screen, not the Overview's): dismissable except while a checkpoint is being written, which ends by itself (CheckpointStatusBanner.tsx:22-31). Unchanged.

D2. The merge row follows the Hub's stall, not a second rule in the browser. The Hub already decides what 'approved work did not reach the product' means: task_transition_service._note_stall raises integration_skipped/failed for every skip or failure except ALREADY_INTEGRATED and stalls.resolve_task_after_commit ends it on merge. The Overview's own rule (status approved and latest_integration.outcome != merged) disagrees with it, and also reads whichever row of a multi-commit approval wins an unordered tie (api/v1/tasks.py:557-578 orders by created_at only). Reading the stall makes the row clear itself, makes Dismiss mean the same thing as for every other stall, and needs no Hub change. The stall row and the merge row stop being two renderings of one fact (OverviewScreen.tsx:157 already folds them).

D3. Settings split by whose they are. App settings: the operator's, for every project on this Hub, kept where they are kept today (notification prefs and mode in localStorage per window, prefs.ts and configStore.ts; the Hub address and key in the config store). Project settings: unchanged sections (ProjectSettingsScreen.tsx:23-33), minus Sound and notifications. Agent settings: unchanged sections (AgentSettingsPage.tsx:53-61). App settings is a new destination in lib/navigation.ts so it works with no project open, rendered on SettingsNavLayout (already shared by the other two). The entry is a Settings control in the rail footer beside Add project (Sidebar.tsx:363 and :462), because the rail is the one surface present on every screen including the zero state; the TopBar gear keeps meaning Project settings. The palette gains settings entries because it has none.

D4. One arbiter for Escape and Tab stays useDialogFocus (F310's defaultPrevented rule). A nested layer claims Escape with preventDefault (the delete confirm, as the blocking-reason panel at TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:796-801 does); the Provider list becomes MenuSelect, the Radix select that held in the 2026-10-23 drive; the palette registers as a layer in useDialogFocus's stack so 'newest layer' is true again. Focus return for controlled Radix dialogs is fixed once in DialogContent rather than per caller, since VaultLibrary opens Add from a file drop with no trigger at all.

D5. Delivery: three tasks in order, each committing hub/ui/src with hub/hub/static/ui (the bundle reaches :8000 on its next reload), built outside the Hub's flows.

Tier 1: UI-only, no migration, no Hub route or contract change.

open_questions.question: Which notices F1045 means: decided from a read-only read of :8000 (28 mender questions nobody waits on, and approved tasks whose newest integration was skipped as already in master), since the finding asked for a screenshot or a read of the sources; the operator can correct it on review.
Questions nobody waits on stay in 'Needs you' with Decline rather than leaving the Overview: a late answer is still delivered, so they remain the operator's to answer or decline.
Where App settings is entered: a Settings control in the rail footer (present with no project open), and the palette; the TopBar gear keeps meaning Project settings.

problem: On 2026-10-25 the operator reported Overview notifications that 'are not dismissable and I have no action to take on them, they are just living there' (F1045). A read-only read of :8000 on 2026-10-27 shows what they are: 28 unanswered questions in proj-d85a82bf4216, all blocking questions from the mender whose wait had ended (27 copies of one question about task-8618731d065d), each offering only 'Open conversation' (OverviewScreen.tsx:102-123); and 22 of the project's 33 approved tasks whose newest integration row is a skip, 19 of them 'already in master' and 12 of them merged by the same approval, each a candidate 'approved but not merged' row with only 'Open task' (OverviewScreen.tsx:140-154) while no integration stall is open. Settings are hard to find: sound and notifications are the operator's own, for every project (NotificationSettings.tsx:17-31), yet sit inside one project's Project settings > General (GeneralSettings.tsx:439), hidden while that project's settings load or fail (GeneralSection.tsx:58-81); with no project open there is no settings entry at all (App.tsx:653), and the palette offers none. The 2026-10-23 keyboard sweep found six focus defects (F1027-F1032), each with a verified cause and a named failing test, still present on master (AgentCreateDialog.tsx:26-115, CommandPalette.tsx:74-87, VaultAddDialog.tsx:131, TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:484-495 and :715-760, PaneResizer.tsx:139-160).

requirements.rationale: F1045: on :8000 on 2026-10-27 the Overview listed 28 questions nobody was waiting on and up to 22 'approved but not merged' rows whose only control was 'Open conversation' or 'Open task'. A row that can only be visited lives forever.
requirements.statement: Every row under the Overview's 'Needs you' offers, on the row itself, at least one control that ends the condition that raised it or dismisses the row (answer or decline a question, resume a blocked task, try a merge again or dismiss it, dismiss a stall, make a fix task for flaky tests or dismiss them). No row offers only navigation.

requirements.rationale: The decline route exists (hub/hub/api/v1/questions.py:640) and the Questions page offers it (QuestionsPanel.tsx:92-105); the Overview does not. 27 of the 28 open questions on :8000 are copies of one mender question whose wait ended.
requirements.statement: Each unanswered question row on the Overview offers Decline, which closes the question through the existing decline route and removes the row. When two or more listed questions have no asker waiting, one control on the section declines all of them after a confirmation that names how many.

requirements.rationale: The Hub already decides which approved work did not reach the product: it records a stall for every skip or failure except 'already in the target' and ends it when the work merges (task_transition_service.py:1308-1337, stalls.py:325-346). The Overview re-derives the rule from latest_integration (OverviewScreen.tsx:140-154) and gets it wrong for 22 of 33 approved tasks on :8000.
requirements.statement: An 'approved but not merged' row is listed only while its task has an open integration_skipped or integration_failed stall, and leaves the Overview when that stall ends (the work merged, the mender fixed it, or the operator dismissed it). A task whose skip says its commit is already in the target branch is never listed. The row offers Try again when the task's latest integration is retryable, and Dismiss, which ends the stall.

requirements.rationale: Resume, Dismiss (stall) and Dismiss (flaky) mutate with no error handler today (OverviewScreen.tsx:137, :172, :201), so a refusal looks like a button that does nothing.
requirements.statement: When an Overview row's action or dismiss is refused by the Hub, the app shows a toast carrying the Hub's reason and the row stays listed.

Every other notice on the Overview either offers an action or clears itself when its cause ends: the 'Couldn't read ... from the Hub' line offers Retry, which refetches the failed reads, and disappears once they answer; the budget notice keeps its link to Budgets and disappears when the budget is no longer exhausted; the 'held by hop budget' chip on an agent row opens Project settings at the hop budget; 'launch not checked' and 'queue not read' disappear once their reads answer.

requirements.rationale: Today the only gear is 'Project settings' (TopBar.tsx:145-155), the TopBar is rendered only with a project open (App.tsx:653), Hub connection sits in the project switcher's menu (TopBar.tsx:94-98) and the palette has no settings entry at all (no match for 'settings' in CommandPalette.tsx).
requirements.statement: An App settings page holds the settings that belong to the operator rather than to a project: Sound and notifications, Appearance (light or dark) and Hub connection. It is reachable from a Settings control in the rail's footer on every screen, including when no project is open, and from the command palette by typing 'settings', 'sound' or 'notifications'.

requirements.rationale: They are the operator's, kept per window for every project (NotificationSettings.tsx:17-31, prefs.ts:3-19), but live inside Project settings > General (GeneralSettings.tsx:439), which renders nothing of them while that project's settings load or after their read fails (GeneralSection.tsx:58-81).
requirements.statement: Sound and notifications appear in App settings and nowhere in Project settings, and they render and save whether or not any project's settings have loaded.

requirements.rationale: An operator looking for sound in Project settings or agent settings is pointed to it from the page they are on.
requirements.statement: App settings, Project settings and an agent's settings each say in their heading whose settings they are (yours on this Hub, this project's, this agent's), and Project settings and agent settings each carry a link to App settings in their section list.

Escape closes only the innermost open layer and returns focus to the control that opened it: with the Add-agent dialog's Provider list open, Escape closes the list and keeps the dialog and its typed name (F1027); with the task drawer's 'Delete this task?' confirm open, Escape cancels the confirm and keeps the drawer, focus on Delete (F1030). In the Provider list, arrow keys move between providers and Enter picks one.
With the command palette open over a dialog or the task drawer, Tab and typed text stay inside the palette; the dialog beneath does not take focus until the palette closes (F1028).

Closing any dialog built on the shared DialogContent by Escape, Cancel or its close button returns focus to the element that was focused when it opened (the Vault's Add and Vault storage buttons, the Jobs archive confirm's opener; F1029). The task drawer's title is reachable with Tab and opened for renaming with Enter, and after the rename is saved or cancelled focus is on the title control (F1031). Focus never falls to the page body after a close.
A focused pane resizer (Resize navigation, Resize conversation) shows its line in the --ring colour in light and dark mode, and its hover colour applies too (F1032).

in_scope: Every Overview 'Needs you' row offering a control that ends or dismisses its cause, with an error toast when the Hub refuses
Decline on Overview question rows, and a confirmed decline-all for questions nobody waits on
The 'approved but not merged' row driven by the open integration stall, with Try again and Dismiss
Retry on the Overview's couldn't-read line; the hop-budget chip linking to its setting
An App settings page (sound and notifications, appearance, Hub connection) reachable from the rail on every screen and from the palette
Sound and notifications moved out of Project settings; each settings page naming whose settings it holds
F1027-F1032: the Provider list, palette over a dialog, focus return from Radix dialogs, the delete confirm's Escape, keyboard rename, the resizer's focus ring
non_goals: Making the mender ask fewer questions or record them as morning notes while the operator is away: slice N (the-mender-wakes-only-for-real-stalls); this slice only lets the operator clear what is already there
Grouping duplicate questions into one row: the decline-all control covers the backlog; fewer duplicates is slice N's

Fixing the unordered tie in api/v1/tasks.py:557-578 (_latest_integrations_by_task) that can show a merged multi-commit approval as skipped in the task drawer: a pre-existing defect, filed to the backlog as a finding rather than carried here, since the Overview no longer reads it for its row
Per-project or per-agent notification rules, or moving notification preferences to the Hub: they stay the operator's, per window, as today
Moving any project or agent setting between scopes, or adding new settings: D (driver, gate level, people, budget cap) adds its own
A UI check in the project's checks: slice L
The spec page's own surfaces: slice F
Other keyboard or focus findings than F1027-F1032

summary: The Overview stops listing things the operator cannot do anything about: every row under 'Needs you' carries a control that ends or dismisses it, questions can be declined there (one at a time or all those nobody waits on), an 'approved but not merged' row follows the Hub's own integration stall so it clears itself when the work lands and is never shown for work already in main, and every other notice either acts or clears itself. Settings get a home split by whose they are: an App settings page, reachable from the rail on every screen and from the palette, holds sound and notifications, appearance and the Hub connection, while Project and agent settings keep their sections and say whose they are. The six keyboard findings F1027-F1032 are fixed so Escape closes one layer, the palette keeps focus over a dialog, closing a dialog returns focus to its opener, a task can be renamed from the keyboard, and a focused resizer is visible.
